notes:
Typing, wrapped links and workspace terminals

• Editing earlier text with the phone keyboard no longer repeats sentences or adds stray characters. Backspacing into a word, moving the cursor and autocorrect now change only the text you edited.
• Inside a workspace, + Terminal starts a new terminal in that workspace.
• A terminal's menu can remove it from its workspace. Its tmux session keeps running.
• Plain shells from the desktop app show as Desktop only, with how to share them, instead of an error and a Reconnect button that could not work.
• A web address that an app wraps onto the next line now opens whole when tapped, as on desktop, instead of stopping at the end of the first line.

Updates from desktop releases

• The app now finds updates in DazeDev desktop releases that include the Android app, as well as in Android-only releases, and offers whichever is newer.
• As before, the download is checked against the release's checksum file before Android installs it.

Built-in SSH, your own agents and a prompt editor

• SSH and Tailscale hosts now use a built-in SSH client. You sign in once per host and every terminal shares that connection. It follows your ~/.ssh/config, checks known_hosts, refuses a changed host key, and uses your SSH agent, key files and certificates. Turn on "Use system OpenSSH" for a host that needs a hardware security key.
• Hosts with fish, nu or tcsh as their login shell now work. Hosts need Python 3.9 or newer, and an older Python is reported clearly.
• DazeDev asks before a host opens a link on your computer, before running a repository's worktree script, and before pasting several lines. Remote clipboard writes show a notice by default.
• Terminal output reaches the window faster, uploads over SSH use larger chunks, and a large reply no longer holds up the connection check.
• App shortcuts can be changed in Settings. Ctrl with a letter now goes to the terminal, so Ctrl+K works in the shell and in nano. Scrollback defaults to 10,000 lines.
• Close anyway appears when a check stops DazeDev from closing. Terminal search no longer refreshes on output from other panes.
• Updates are swapped in safely, old update and runtime copies are cleaned up, and startup no longer rewrites permissions on every data file.
• Native PowerShell sessions stream output instead of polling and check who owns the session pipe.
• Dictation keeps long text when the tidy-up changes wording, and shows unsent text in a banner with Send anyway, Copy and Discard.
• Settings files saved with a UTF-8 byte order mark load correctly.
• Typing in a detached terminal window goes straight to the terminal instead of through the main window.
• WSL and local hosts use the faster connection protocol. Uploads send several larger chunks at once.
• Settings and workspace changes save automatically.
• Terminal colours, including the 16 ANSI colours, follow the theme.
• All open terminals share one scrollback and image memory limit, so many terminals cannot use unlimited memory.
• Bad data from a host or settings file shows a clear error.
• The voice runtime is updated to ONNX Runtime 1.23.2, and its usage telemetry is turned off.
• Add your own agent with a name, a launch command and optional install, detection and version commands. It appears in Agents, New session, the command palette and terminal labels. Custom agents are saved on the host, so every desktop and phone connected to it sees them.
• More agents to install and start: GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Qwen Code, Factory Droid, goose, Amp, Crush, Aider and Kimi Code.
• Pastes of up to about 2,000 characters show as text in Codex instead of a "[Pasted Content N chars]" placeholder. Longer pastes open an editable preview first, and nothing is sent until you choose Paste.
• Ctrl+G in Codex and Claude Code opens the prompt in a DazeDev edit pane. Save sends it back to the agent, Cancel leaves it unchanged, and Terminal editor continues in your own editor. Sessions DazeDev starts point $VISUAL and $EDITOR at the DazeDev editor and keep yours as the fallback. Agents started before this update need a restart.
• When this desktop cannot show the editor (only the phone is attached, the terminal is in its own window, or the connection dropped), the terminal editor opens straight away.
• A terminal status error no longer appears when a host returns an unexpected status reply.
• Linux: test .deb and AppImage packages for Linux Mint 21.x and 22.x, built on Ubuntu 22.04. Installed copies keep settings in ~/.local/share/DazeDev, microphone input works in the Linux webview, and updates are manual.
• The first start no longer shows a "device_load reply was malformed" error, and opening DazeDev right after closing it waits for the closing copy instead of failing.

Upload focus hotfix

• Return keyboard focus to the originating terminal when closing Upload, after pasting a path or cancelling.
• Keep the next keystroke in the terminal instead of reopening the upload dialog.

Session exit and recovery

• Return to a usable terminal when Ctrl+C ends an agent.
• Show Open terminal and Close view when a tmux pane has ended, including after reconnecting.
• Recover only the ended pane without restarting the agent or stopping live sessions.
• Show the verified terminal type after an agent exits.

Terminal title hotfix

• Update a plain SSH shell’s terminal name and session type when it enters tmux.
• Follow tmux session renames and switches in main and detached windows.
• Restore the shell label when leaving tmux.

Files, links, broadcast and reconnect on return

• Returning to the app checks each connected host first. A host that stopped answering shows Disconnected with the reason instead of a frozen terminal. Hosts that need no typed password reconnect and reopen the terminal by themselves; the others offer Reconnect, which asks for the password and reopens the same session. Typed input is never resent.
• Stay connected in the background: Off, 5 minutes (the default), 15 minutes, 1 hour or Until I disconnect. The notification counts down and offers Disconnect all; when the time ends, hosts disconnect and the app tells you why when you return.
• Hosts show Disconnected as soon as the phone loses its network, and reconnect when it returns. The screen you were on comes back after Android closes the app, and Back follows one history.
• Private keys are stored encrypted with the Android Keystore, with an optional saved passphrase, so hosts can reconnect without you.
• Upload files to a host from the terminal menu, Share to DazeDev or the clipboard, then paste the path.
• Tap links and file paths in terminal output to open, copy or preview them. Text, Markdown, HTML and image previews are read-only, and nothing opens in the browser until you tap Open.
• Find in the terminal, with match case and regular expressions. Share or save terminal output, and clear the phone's scrollback.
• Broadcast a message or voice draft to several terminals after reviewing the recipients. Each session gets it once.
• Repositories: clone from GitHub and create worktrees on a host.
• Completion alerts show a badge, with optional notifications while the app is in the background (off by default).
• The dictation dictionary corrects voice drafts, with optional sync through a host.
• New session lists every agent the host reports, including custom agents added on desktop.
• The extra-keys row appears only while the keyboard is open and scrolls sideways to reach every key; a key fires only on a tap, never on a swipe. The Keys panel works the same way. Keys above keyboard in settings hides the row. A terminal size option keeps other devices' size when the keyboard opens.
• Faster host connection (protocol 2). In-app updates are checked against the release's SHA256SUMS before installing.
• Updated Kotlin to 2.4.21 (CVE-2026-53914) and JSch to 2.28.8.

Scrolling, connection and security fixes

• Scrolling no longer freezes a tmux pane on every device. A drag scrolls the program, as a mouse wheel does on desktop, so agent history scrolls on the phone.
• "Latest output" appears as a button whenever you scroll back.
• Timeouts show an error instead of leaving "Connecting terminal…" on screen. A lost link shows Disconnected with a Reconnect button.
• Sessions appear as soon as they load, and a session that ended or restarted can be reopened by name.
• The terminal opens at the phone's size. Rotating or briefly switching apps keeps it open.
• A changed SSH host key is refused, and saved host keys can be viewed and forgotten.
• Links a host opens ask first. Missing Python or tmux on a host is reported clearly.
• Ed25519 keys work on every Android version. An extra-keys row adds Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt and arrows.
• A "Private screen" setting hides the app from screenshots and Recents.
• Terminal output is faster, and voice keeps its model loaded and waits for the last words.
• This is the first release build. It is smaller, not debuggable, and signed with a new release key that phones running alpha.6 accept as an update.

Browser opening hotfix

• Open web links from terminal output in the phone browser.
• Forward browser requests from newly started remote agents and shells to Android.
• Keep the mobile terminal scrollback fix from alpha.5.

Existing agents started without browser forwarding need a restart to inherit it. Localhost callback forwarding remains unavailable.

Terminal scrollback hotfix

• Drag down in a terminal to read earlier output, then drag up to return.
• Scroll attached tmux history without sending keys to the running app.
• Keep long-press text selection and return to live output with Latest.

Privacy and reliability fixes

• Keep local voice requests on loopback, bypass proxies and refuse redirects.
• Protect app-owned settings and recovery files with private permissions.
• Prevent duplicate terminal replies across detached views.
• Bound terminal search and keep host discovery responsive.
• Update dependency fixes and reduce editor and highlight overhead.

Workspace and input controls

• Copy selected terminal text with Ctrl+C without interrupting the session.
• Reorder hosts, expand their workspaces with one click and fit more rows in the sidebar.
• Group terminals into tabs and clone persistent terminal views into hostless workspaces.
• Discover voice shortcuts on first Listen and double-tap the toggle hotkey to submit reviewed dictation.
• Read desktop and mobile release history together.
• Explain unsupported Windows Tailscale SSH targets and distinguish unknown host keys from changed keys.

Workspaces and navigation

• Use the DazeDev home layout with host sections, workspace menus and credits at the bottom.
• Drag workspace handles to reorder the host profile.
• Group terminals as tabs and collect existing terminal views in hostless workspaces on the phone.
• Read the global changelog with platform filters.
• Check the public GitHub repository for Android APK updates; offline development installs remain available.
• Keep the first-tap listening and Enter-to-close voice flow.

Voice input

• Tap Voice to open a blank prompt and start listening.
• Tap End to stop and edit, or Enter to submit once and return to the terminal.
• Keep the draft when delivery fails or the terminal changes.

Updates

• Download signed Windows updates from GitHub Releases over HTTPS.
• Use configured HTTP proxies when checking and downloading updates.

Fixes

• Keep unchanged runtime files in place during updates so files still in use do not block installation.
• Check changed files for locks before replacing the app and retry short Windows file locks.
• Identify the blocked file if installation cannot continue.

Major features

• Search live terminals in the current terminal, workspace, host or all hosts. Browse scrollable results, then use Enter and Shift+Enter to move between matches across workspaces with a compact search bar. Search uses current terminal buffers without saving content or query history.

• Drag workspaces to reorder them within a host in the sidebar.

• Keep repository and tmux controls visible as terminal headers narrow, then reduce them to tmux and the menu, and finally the menu alone.

Improvements

Improvements

Improvements

Major features
